claim: An interrupted (effect_pending) tool call may be replayed only when BOTH the persisted call policy (ToolCall.replay) and the current tool declaration (AgentHarnessTool.replay) are 'safe' and the run is not cancelled; otherwise the interrupted outcome is published with the durable checkpoint, leaving it in place and never invoking the tool.
claim_citations: packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts:295-330 (clearReplayCheckpoint: only the replay path deletes the pending tool output and re-invokes)
packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts:158-168 (interruptedOutcome: durable checkpoint prefix plus the interruption marker)
packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts:331-340 (readCheckpoint: the interrupted path reads, never clears, the checkpoint)
packages/agent/src/harness/pico3/kinds/tool.ts:137 (equivalent kernel rule: interrupt unless both policies are safe)

changes.description: recoverToolInvocation() combined the two safety declarations with `||`, so a persisted 'safe' call policy alone (or a current 'safe' declaration alone) authorized replay of an interrupted tool. Now replay requires both declarations to be safe and no cancellation.

Standalone Node assertion script that drives the real recoverToolInvocation through a test-only trailer and fakes for the lane/session/execution boundaries; asserts replay only for the doubly-safe, uncancelled case and interrupted-with-checkpoint for every other combination.

validation.notes: Ran from the workspace root with Node v24.14.0; exit 0 after the repair. The script loads the production file packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts through .prale-eval/subject.mjs createGraph() (TypeScript stripping + VM modules) with a test-only trailer exposing the private recoverToolInvocation, and supplies its own boundary fakes (lane command/settleOperation/emitBatch/hooks, session value addresses plus a reader over durable values, openToolProgress, tool-placement helpers, executeToolCall/finalizeToolCall/createToolResultMessage). Covered scenarios: (a) persisted safe + declared safe, uncancelled -> the tool is re-invoked once, the pending checkpoint is deleted exactly once, one recovery tool_start carries the persisted arguments, result is not an error; (b) persisted safe + declared never; (c) persisted never + declared safe; (d) persisted never + declared never; (e) persisted safe + declaration defaulting to undefined; (f) persisted safe + tool no longer registered; (g) persisted safe + declared safe + cancel_requested -> each of (b)-(g) asserts zero executions, zero checkpoint-clearing writes, zero replay tool_start events, exactly one recovery tool_end with isError, and an outcome carrying the durable checkpoint content ('durable partial') plus checkpoint details ({ progress: 'kept' }) and the interruption marker text. Fault sensitivity was confirmed by temporarily restoring the original `||` condition in place: the script then failed with `AssertionError: persisted safe + declared never: the interrupted tool was invoked` (actual ['write-file'] vs expected []), and it passed again after re-applying the fix. Limitations: repository dependencies are not installed in this sandbox, so `npm`/`vitest` suites (e.g. packages/agent/test/harness/runtime/drive-tools.test.ts) could not be executed; the regression instead exercises the production module directly with no external dependencies, and prints only ExperimentalWarning lines for stripTypeScriptTypes/VM modules on stderr.
